text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds chalked up strong gains in late trade, lifted by a rise in U.S. Treasuries following a stronger-than-expected fall in the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management index (NAPM). The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.06, up 0.40 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts locked in a half-point gain on Tuesday, dragged upward by a rally in U.S. Treasuries prompted by an unexpectedly large fall in the September NAPM, but traders warned the gains made by gilts and other markets may be overdone and profit-taking could characterise the early house of Wednesday trade. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-05/32, up 18/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French December bond futures were buoyed late in the session by rallies in the German and U.S. bond markets to post a new contract closing high, a weaker-than-expected U.S. National Association of Purchasing Managers survey sent the December contract to 125.10, just shy of the intra-day contract high at 125.14, and it settled at 125.08. The previous closing high was 124.84. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 125.08, up 0.26 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt futures reversed early losses to trade higher in late afternoon taking their lead from higher T-bonds and bunds after a fall in the U.S. NAPM index. The data showed the U.S. economy slightly weaker than forecast and prompted an upturn in Treasuries which was quickly followed by BTPs and bunds. A recovery in the lira added support. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 122.11, up 0.62 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices were higher at midday on Tuesday, having advanced after an index of businesss conditions in the nation's manufacturing sector pointed to moderate growth and no extreme price pressures. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-24/32, up 18/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.89 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended the Tokyo session easier after a denial by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of Ministry of Finance's (MOF) International Finance Bureau, that he had said Japan was not likely to raise interest rates until the end of March, 1997. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.17, up 0.02 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Argentina launched a $750 million 10-year global bond which will be priced tomorrow to yield 445 to 450 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. Initial feedback was positive. An official at joint lead manager Salomon Brothers said the deal was already oversubscribed. The paper was targeted at institutional investors.
